slice_scope: ALL THREE SLICES, shipped as one guardrail. Re-scoped 2026-08-01 by operator decision: Slice 01 alone detects drift and still writes the contaminated roster, which does not meet the requirement ("I don't want to just detect something but not act on it because I'd have the same issue again"). Slices 01-03 now deploy together.
scope_change_note: The DEVOPS D11 7-day soak between Slice 01 and Slice 03 was premised on a risk that no longer exists. Its purpose was to catch a binding adopted from an ALREADY-DRIFTED key at deploy time — trust-on-first-use would cement the wrong identity behind a green tick. The operator has remediated the incident and every registered key now resolves to its correct guild, so the first probe binds correctly by construction. The residual risk the soak addressed (intermittent drift) is separately bounded by DDD-6: an outage classifies UNREACHABLE and a dropped guildId classifies UNVERIFIABLE, neither of which quarantines. Only a well-formed 200 returning a DIFFERENT guildId does. Operator must still eyeball the first-bind announcements on the first post-deploy cycle.
non_goals: player_registrations.api_key — out of scope per DISCUSS; /registration validate_keys covers liveness there
Contaminated-data remediation — no purge command, no is_former cleanup (DISCUSS Out of Scope)
Automatic key recovery — a quarantined guild stays quarantined until a human installs a key
build_order_constraint: Slice 02 MUST be implemented before Slice 03 (DISCUSS D3 / ADR-008 D3). /update_guild_key is the ONLY exit from quarantine. Building enforcement first means the first quarantine is unrecoverable without SSH, with updates also stopped — worse than the bug being fixed. This constraint governs BUILD order; it no longer implies separate deploys.

validation.gate: orchestrator automated gate 2026-08-01: AC coupling clean, decomposition ratio 9 steps / 15 files = 0.60, no identical patterns, no validation-only steps, all ids match ^\d{2}-\d{2}$, every step carries test_file + scenario_name

phases.name: Probe foundations
phases.description: Enforcement made real, structured records made shareable, and the one module that talks to Tacticus.

steps.name: Pin the enforcement tools and add the fifth contract
criteria: requirements.txt pins import-linter and pytest-archon
pyproject.toml gains a contract forbidding bot.repository* from importing bot.guild_keys
lint-imports reports 5 contracts kept, 0 broken
steps.implementation_notes: DEVOPS D10. Do NOT pin hypothesis: its only consumer is tier_b/, which exercises the Slice 03 quarantine state machine. Pinning it here turns a documented skip into a failure. Pin unversioned to match the file's existing style. The fifth contract mirrors the direction of DESIGN rule 4 — policy depends on storage, never the reverse.

steps.name: Promote the structured log helper to bot/obs.py
criteria: bot/obs.py emit_structured writes one single-line JSON record
bot/obs.py imports json and logging only
bot/db/session.py imports the helper rather than defining its own
existing db.* records keep their current shape
steps.implementation_notes: DEVOPS U1. PROMOTE _emit_structured verbatim, do not rewrite it — two divergent JSON log schemas is exactly what structured logging exists to prevent, and every KPI query in kpi-contracts.yaml assumes one shape. Fields must also be attached to the LogRecord as attributes so a test can assert record.event without re-parsing the line; the conftest key_events fixture reads them that way. Keep the module import-light: bot/guild_keys.py is imported by three cogs and a service, and importing session.py from it would drag SQLAlchemy onto the JSON rollback path.

steps.name: Implement the Tacticus guild client
criteria: parse_guild_snapshot returns MATCH-eligible identity plus members from one payload
a payload with no guildId classifies UNVERIFIABLE and never compares guildTag
a missing guildTag or name still yields an identity
401 and 403 classify DEAD; timeout, connection error and 5xx classify UNREACHABLE
members equal the set the old _fetch_roster produced
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-2 and DDD-10. fetch_guild_snapshot must NEVER raise for an expected failure — transport errors, 5xx and dead-key statuses all return a classified snapshot, because the caller's whole job is to tell them apart and an exception erases the distinction. Import httpx INSIDE the function, not at module scope, so the module stays import-light. Remove __SCAFFOLD__. The two @requires_external scenarios stay skipped unless SCRAPCODE_TACTICUS_CONTRACT_KEY is set; do not weaken them to make them run.

phases.name: The binding store (US-006)
phases.description: A table of its own, reachable only through the repository port.

steps.name: Add the binding row and its Alembic revision
criteria: GuildKeyBindingRow is 1:1 with guilds, FK ondelete CASCADE
revision sets down_revision to 0002
upgrade creates an empty guild_key_bindings and alters no guilds row or column
downgrade restores the prior schema exactly
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-4. Columns: tacticus_guild_id (the binding), tacticus_guild_tag and tacticus_guild_name (display only), identity_bound_at, key_status, quarantine_reason, quarantined_at, last_alerted_at. No backfill — trust-on-first-use populates it, so downgrade is a plain drop_table. quarantined_at MUST be ISO-8601 UTC in the SAME string shape as battle_hits.completed_on (String(32), stored verbatim from Tacticus): KPI-2 compares them as strings and a shape mismatch returns a wrong result set silently instead of erroring. Confirm the real completed_on format against a production row before relying on it. Adding columns to guilds is a test failure, not an alternative.

steps.name: Extend the repository port and both adapters
criteria: ABC gains load_guild_binding, save_guild_binding, list_guild_bindings
SQLite adapter reads and writes guild_key_bindings
JSON adapter reports unbound and no-ops the write without raising
bot/guilds.py exposes thin wrappers over the three methods
Guild dataclass and save_guilds are unchanged
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-007 pattern. The JSON adapter degrading to unbound is deliberate, not a stub — ADR-006 D9 rollback must leave the feature inert rather than raising. bot/guilds.py already carries the three wrapper scaffolds; implement them in place and remove __SCAFFOLD__. Touching the Guild dataclass is the specific hazard DDD-4 exists to prevent: save_guilds rebuilds Guild from a five-key dict, so a binding field added there would be overwritten with None by any unrelated admin command. bot/guilds.py must not import bot.guild_keys or httpx — asserted by a test that passes today.

phases.name: Policy and wiring (US-001, US-002)
phases.description: The chokepoint, the roster refactor, and the six guild-key call sites routed through it. Reports everything, blocks nothing.

steps.name: Implement the key policy chokepoint
criteria: first successful probe adopts the identity and stamps identity_bound_at
a later probe refreshes the date and does not re-announce
mismatch is classified on guildId alone; a retag or rename is not a mismatch
dead, unreachable and unverifiable each leave the stored binding byte-identical
active_key is sync and makes no network call
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-1, DDD-6, DDD-8, DDD-10. verify_and_resolve ships with enforce=False and NO caller passes True in this slice — quarantine is Slice 03 and shipping the block before the recovery path violates ADR-008 D3. quarantine() and release() may stay unimplemented; they are Slice 02/03. Only uuid is ever compared: tag and name are display, so a legitimate retag must not trip the lock. Emit guild.key.bound, guild.key.probe.ok, guild.key.mismatch, guild.key.unverifiable, guild.key.unreachable, guild.key.dead through bot/obs.py, each carrying key_ref — the first 8 hex of api_key_hmac, never the key. KPI-6 is zero by construction, not by filtering.

steps.name: Move the roster fetch out of the Chronicler package
criteria: _fetch_roster is deleted
refresh_guild and validate_if_stale take a GuildSnapshot, not an api_key
bot/services/chronicl3r no longer imports httpx
Chronicler profile calls are unchanged
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-2. Delete, do not deprecate — an httpx import left behind is the signal that a second unguarded call path survived the move, which is what these two tests exist to catch. The members frozenset on GuildSnapshot must be the same set _fetch_roster returned; a contract scenario asserts exactly that. PlayerService keeps every Chronicler call it has: only the Tacticus call leaves.

steps.name: Route the hourly loop through the chokepoint
criteria: auto_update verifies each guild before ingesting and still writes on a mismatch
first bind posts exactly one message naming the guild and adopted identity
a matching guild produces no message in any channel and no alert record
the mismatch line appears in the summary beside the healthy guilds
auto_update.cycle records guilds_total, guilds_processed, guilds_skipped and skip_reasons
steps.implementation_notes: AC-002.2 — this slice REPORTS and still ingests. An implementation that blocks passes the drift scenarios and fails test_slice_01_still_ingests_on_a_mismatch, which is the scenario protecting the D3 slice order. test_a_matching_guild_is_completely_silent is the one scenario an unconditionally-alerting implementation fails, and it is the empirical basis for KPI-4; do not weaken it. Season discovery moves to active_key with fall-through (DDD-7) so the tasks_cog:174 read leaves. cap_detect at line 75 reads a PLAYER key and is out of scope — leave it exactly as it is. Detection latency is alerted_at minus last_probe_ok_at (DEVOPS U2), so guild.key.probe.ok must carry a parseable timestamp.

steps.name: Route the remaining key reads and render the binding
criteria: update_leaderboard and update_all resolve keys through the chokepoint
set_live_leaderboard and set_live_cluster_leaderboard do the same
/view_config shows the bound tag, the first 8 characters of the identifier and the verification date
a guild with no key still renders exactly as it did before
no cog reads a guild api_key directly
steps.implementation_notes: Closes DESIGN rule 1 for guild keys. After this step the chokepoint scan must report zero offenders. admin_cog:183 is a presence check feeding the existing Missing rendering that AC-005.3 pins as unchanged — the scan exempts it structurally, so leave its shape alone; binding state renders alongside it, not instead of it. A missing tag or name renders as a dash and must never block the bind (AC-001.6). No identifier longer than 8 characters may appear in any embed.

steps.name: Close the environment matrix
criteria: a clean cluster binds all three guilds and announces once, then stays silent
a fully bound, matching cluster raises no alert of any kind
an identifier missing cluster-wide alerts loudly and still ingests everywhere
an outage leaves every binding byte-identical across the whole cluster
a revoked key is reported as dead and the operator is told to install a new one
steps.implementation_notes: Mandate 4, Environmental Realism. These are whole-cluster properties over the six Slice 01 environments, not repeats of the single-guild scenarios: each drives auto_update across a cluster and asserts the environment's headline invariant. Expect most to pass once 03-01..03-04 are green — treat any that does not as a real defect in the per-guild logic that only shows up in aggregate, which is the entire reason this layer exists. bound-drifted and mixed-cluster are deliberately NOT here: both assert quarantine, which is Slice 03. The last two names are regression guards that pass today and must still pass at the end.

phases.name: The recovery path — /update_guild_key (US-003, Slice 02)
phases.description: The only exit from quarantine. Ships BEFORE enforcement so the exit provably exists before the entrance opens.

steps.name: Write a guild key and clear quarantine
criteria: a key write updates api_key and api_key_hmac in one transaction
release clears key_status, quarantine_reason and quarantined_at
the stored key is unchanged when a probe does not succeed
no key value reaches any log record
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-006 D7: api_key is Fernet ciphertext and api_key_hmac is a deterministic HKDF-SHA256 derivation carrying a UNIQUE constraint. BOTH must be produced in the SAME transaction — a write that updates one without the other leaves a row whose uniqueness check no longer matches its key. Raw-SQL key edits are forbidden. AC-003.2 is the property that makes this command safe where /deregister_guild is not: players, battle_hits and bomb_hits counts must be IDENTICAL before and after, so nothing may CASCADE. release() currently raises NotImplementedError as a deliberate slice boundary; implement it here — quarantine must never be a trap (DISCUSS D3), and this is the slice that proves the exit exists before Slice 03 opens the entrance.

steps.name: Add the /update_guild_key command
criteria: the key is probed BEFORE it is stored and the reply names the resolved guild
a key resolving to a different guild is refused without force and installed with it
dead and unverifiable keys are refused and the stored key is unchanged
officer tier is refused and the probe never fires
the reply is ephemeral and contains no key value
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-9: a `force: bool` PARAMETER, not a stateful confirmation. A discord.ui.View button would hold the plaintext key in process memory until click or timeout, which is a KPI-6 leak surface with a several-minute window. Probe the SUBMITTED key before storing anything — never install a key that could not be verified (AC-003.6). Tier is admin, matching /register_guild, via the real @require_tier decorator (ADR-001); officer is deliberately insufficient because the key grants read access to a guild's full roster and raid history. test_an_officer_cannot_replace_a_guild_key additionally asserts the probe NEVER fired — otherwise the command is an oracle for whether an arbitrary key is valid. Reuse bot/embeds.py:guild_autocomplete unchanged.

phases.name: Enforcement — quarantine (US-004, US-005, Slice 03)
phases.description: The guardrail itself. A drifted key writes zero rows, and quarantining one guild does not stop any other.

steps.name: Quarantine on drift and rate-limit the alert
criteria: a mismatch sets key_status quarantined and records both identities and the moment
verify_and_resolve honours enforce=True and raises GuildQuarantined before any request
an outage or a missing identifier never quarantines anything
at most one alert per guild per 24 hours while the state persists
suppressed alerts are recorded, not dropped silently
steps.implementation_notes: quarantine() currently raises NotImplementedError as a deliberate slice boundary — implement it, and flip verify_and_resolve to honour enforce=True. quarantined_at MUST be ISO-8601 UTC in the SAME String(32) shape as battle_hits.completed_on; KPI-2's query compares them AS STRINGS and a shape mismatch returns a wrong result set silently rather than erroring. DDD-6 is the decision that keeps a Tacticus outage from quarantining the whole cluster: only a well-formed 200 carrying a DIFFERENT guildId quarantines. UNREACHABLE, UNVERIFIABLE and DEAD must each leave key_status untouched. GuildQuarantined must raise BEFORE any request is made — fetching the other guild's data and then discarding it puts it in memory and possibly in a traceback. ALERT_SUPPRESSION_HOURS = 24 via last_alerted_at; the FIRST alert of a quarantine always fires.

steps.name: Block every write for a quarantined guild
criteria: no battle-hit or bomb-hit row is written for a quarantined guild
no player row is inserted, updated or flipped to former
all seven key-consumption sites refuse and make no request
the alert reaches the update channel and the guild ping channel
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-5: quarantine blocks roster AND hits. Blocking only hits still lets refresh_guild invert the roster, which was 60 of the 67 corrupted players rows — the LARGER half of the damage. test_every_key_consumption_site_refuses_a_quarantined_guild is parametrized over the seven-member KeyConsumptionSite enum AND asserts call_count == 0, so an implementation that fetches the other guild's data and then discards it still fails. This is the step where test_slice_01_still_ingests_on_a_mismatch INVERTS: it asserted the non-blocking intermediate state deliberately, and Slice 03 is where that stops being true. Do NOT delete it — report it to the orchestrator, which owns the decision about how to record the inversion.

steps.name: Keep one guild's quarantine from stopping the server
criteria: season discovery skips a quarantined guild and uses the next usable key
a healthy guild beside a quarantined one updates normally
a server whose guilds are all quarantined is skipped with a stated reason
the cycle records how many guilds it processed and skipped
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-7 / KPI-5, and the reason active_key exists as a separate sync entry point. auto_update derived the season from next(iter(guilds.values())) and skipped the ENTIRE server when that one key failed — so quarantining one guild would have halted every guild, which is worse than the bug being fixed. The fall-through was written in step 03-03 and is dormant because nothing could be quarantined; this step is where it becomes reachable and must be proven. The fixture pins the quarantined guild FIRST in dict order and asserts that precondition, because the SPOF only misbehaves in that ordering — a test that happens to put it second passes while the bug is fully present. An all-quarantined server must be skipped with an explicit reason, never a silent continue.

steps.name: Show quarantine state in the guild list
criteria: a quarantined guild shows the state, both tags and the quarantine date
an active bound guild shows a tick, its tag and the verification date
a guild with no key reads exactly as it did before this feature
no key value and no identifier beyond eight characters appears
steps.implementation_notes: US-005. The officer's job here is to tell the difference between 'nothing happened this hour' and 'this guild is blocked and needs an admin'. AC-005.3 pins the existing Missing rendering as UNCHANGED for a keyless guild — admin_cog:183 must stay an If/IfExp test or the architecture scan's structural exemption stops applying and correctly starts failing. Step 03-04 noted identity-label rendering is now duplicated across tasks_cog, admin_cog and update_cog; consolidating it into bot/guild_keys.py alongside key_ref is in scope for this step if it does not widen the diff unreasonably.

steps.name: Close the enforcement environments and the state machine
criteria: bound-drifted writes nothing once enforcement is on
mixed-cluster survives a quarantined first guild
quarantine is never a trap — every quarantined state has a path back to active
a quarantined guild never writes under any interleaving
steps.implementation_notes: The last two environment scenarios, plus the Tier B layer that has been skipping since DISTILL. Pin hypothesis in requirements.txt NOW — this is the slice its state machine exercises, so the skip stops being honest and starts being missing coverage. tier_b/test_key_status_state_machine.py asserts two whole-state-space properties no enumerated example establishes: quarantine_is_never_a_trap (from every reachable quarantined state there EXISTS a path back to active — DISCUSS D3 is exactly this claim, and a single example only shows that one path works) and quarantined_guilds_never_write (zero rows under every interleaving of probes and key updates, not just the orderings someone thought to write). Plus one negative test per Hebert ch.6: relax 'the admin installs a matching key' and the property must FAIL without force, or the force gate is decorative.
